walkthroughs.body_html: Muhammad was born in Mecca in 570 CE. He worked as a merchant, known for being honest and trustworthy. At about age 40, he began receiving revelations from God (Allah) through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) — these became the Quran.

Muhammad faced opposition in Mecca, so in 622 CE he and his followers moved to Medina. This journey is called the Hijra and marks the start of the Muslim calendar. In Medina he built the first Muslim community.

By the time Muhammad died in 632 CE, much of Arabia had become Muslim. Within a century, Islam spread across the Middle East, North Africa and into Asia and Europe. Today there are about 1.9 billion Muslims worldwide.
